newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says ASEAN position on WTO well known.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says ASEAN position on WTO well known.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Saturday the position of the seven-nation Southeast Asian group towards world trade talks in Singapore next month was solid and well known.
He indicated that the meeting of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) opening in Singapore on December 8 had not come up during an informal one-day annual summit of ASEAN leaders in Jakarta.
Asked whether the WTO had been discussed, he told a news conference: "The ASEAN position on the WTO is quite solid and well known and there was no need to elaborate further."

ASEAN, which groups Indonesian, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, Brunei and the Philippines, is strongly opposed to the introduction of what it regards as non-trade issues at the inaugural ministerial meeting of the WTO, the global trade regulatory body.
ASEAN ministers on the sidelines of the summit said they were set for tough talks at the Singapore conference.
"Our positions on these issues will be substantially maintained," Philippine Foreign Minister Domingo Siazon said.
The United States and some other Western powers are seeking to add to the agenda such issues as labour standards, investment guarantees, competition policy and textile markets.
"Our positions on these issues will be substantially maintained," Philippine Foreign Minister Domingo Siazon said.
